test_title: Delhi Police Constable (Executive) 2023 - GK/CA (Held on: 29 Nov, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: gk
question: In which of the following cases does revenue deficit occur?

options.text: When the government’s total revenue exceeds its expenditure
When the government’s revenue is added to its expenditure
When the government’s total revenue is less than its expenditure
When the government’s total revenue is equal to its expenditure

solution:
The correct answer is __**When the government’s total revenue is less than its expenditure**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A revenue deficit occurs when the **government's total revenue receipts are less than its total revenue expenditure**.
 
• It indicates that the government is unable to cover its regular operational expenses through its revenue receipts.
 
• **Revenue receipts** include income from taxes (direct and indirect) and non-tax revenues like profits from public sector enterprises and dividends.
 
• **Revenue expenditure** refers to spending on day-to-day operations such as salaries, subsidies, interest payments, and administrative costs.
 
• A persistent revenue deficit is considered unhealthy for the economy as it compels the government to borrow or cut into its capital expenditures, which affects developmental activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fiscal Deficit:**

 
 
• It represents the total borrowing requirements of the government.
 
• Fiscal deficit occurs when the total expenditure of the government exceeds its total receipts (excluding borrowings).
 
• A high fiscal deficit indicates excessive government borrowing, which can lead to inflation or debt issues.
 
 
 
• **Primary Deficit:**
 
 
• Primary deficit is calculated as the fiscal deficit minus interest payments on previous borrowings.
 
• It reflects the borrowing requirements of the government excluding interest obligations.
 
 
 
• **Capital Expenditure:**
 
 
• It refers to government spending on creating assets such as infrastructure, education facilities, and health services.
 
• Unlike revenue expenditure, capital expenditure contributes to long-term economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Ways to Reduce Revenue Deficit:**
 
 
• Improving tax collection efficiency and increasing tax base.
 
• Reducing unnecessary subsidies and controlling administrative costs.
 
• Encouraging privatization or monetization of government assets.
